object_description: compact multi-storey volume flanking a new campus square
design_condition: The building establishes a new central square between existing institutions, adopts the existing campus levels and architecture, and connects the surrounding pedestrian routes, although the square edge and accessible level changes remain unresolved.

positive.statement: The urban development creates a new center and convincingly interlinks the new building with the existing buildings.

position.rationale: Central open area and adjoining mass suggest the new square linking surrounding campus buildings.

positive.statement: The large square integrates well with the street axis and fits into the existing campus topography.

position.rationale: Top view identifies the open forecourt; elevations confirm its ground-level relationship to the stepped building.

positive.statement: The elegant facade structure adopts the existing design language and strengthens the educational ensemble.

position.rationale: Regular elevated facade grid is clearly visible across the taller volume.

positive.statement: The clear facade division responds to floor functions and makes the individual uses visible from outside.

position.rationale: Horizontal floor bands and differing lower and upper volumes visibly divide the facade.

positive.statement: The compact building shape enables a simple and functional floor plan.

position.rationale: Orthogonal compact mass and stepped profile are consistently visible in all calibrated views.

positive.statement: The clear geometry guarantees flexibility and supports a variety of housing types.

position.rationale: Uniform point spacing and rectilinear massing support the broad flexibility and layout assessment.

positive.statement: Regular window placement provides good daylight and views in several directions.

position.rationale: Repeated window points form clearly regular vertical and horizontal facade fields.

positive.statement: The calm design with irregularly distributed green islands enables the preservation of valuable existing trees.

position.rationale: Landscape islands are suggested around the low front edge, though individual trees are not distinguishable.

positive.statement: The continuous grid and rationally sized structural system support economical construction.

position.rationale: Repeated point rows visibly indicate a rational structural rhythm through the building mass.

negative.statement: The connection on the institutional side is not convincingly solved, and the proposed ramps are not possible as shown.

position.rationale: The eastern building edge is visible, but the specific institutional connection and ramp geometry are unresolved.

negative.statement: It is questionable whether the square should extend to the facade where adjacent uses have no relation to it.

position.rationale: Approximate square-to-facade interface is placed along the front of the taller volume.

negative.statement: The need to fell distinctive existing trees is incomprehensible.

position.rationale: Likely tree-island locations are estimated in the open low-density portion of the site.

negative.statement: The continued passability of the square is suggested because no turning options are shown.

position.rationale: Open ground area is visible, but turning and circulation options are not represented distinctly.

negative.statement: The trails leading away from the street add little quality of stay while sealing additional green spaces.

position.rationale: Approximate paths and landscape edge are assigned to the sparse southern site perimeter.

negative.statement: The building statics do not work consistently from bottom to top because an upper load-bearing wall lacks adequate support.

position.rationale: Upper wall region is visible, but load transfer and support conditions cannot be verified from points.

negative.statement: The high glass facade wings should open onto the square for summer use.

position.rationale: Tall facade wings are identifiable, while glazing and their relationship to the square remain uncertain.

negative.statement: A covered outdoor space usable regardless of weather is missing.

position.rationale: A possible ground-level edge zone is estimated beside the square; no canopy is distinctly sampled.

negative.statement: The water treatment is unclear and appears as an unwanted depression in the tree islands.

position.rationale: Tree-island depressions may occupy this open landscape area, but water elements are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The apartment access through the stairwell and narrow elevator vestibule is too small and will not function optimally.

position.target: apartment access stairwell and elevator vestibule
position.rationale: Access is approximated along the lower facade edge; interior stair and vestibule geometry is not visible.

negative.statement: The internal organization and routing on the upper public floor still require optimization.

position.target: upper public floor organization and routing
position.rationale: The upper storey is clearly located in the tall block, though internal organization is concealed.

negative.statement: Audience and operating rooms are not clearly separated.

position.rationale: Likely public-service zones are approximated within the tall front-facing volume; room separation is not visible.
